recommendation: Keep the no-change audit. If FHIR-I wants the target-resource/simple-type details to be made more explicit again, handle that as follow-up in the cross-version package guidance or FAQ rather than as a core source reconciliation for FHIR-36702.
issue_request: FHIR-36702 was a Published/Persuasive with Modification FHIR-I change request asking for clearer guidance that inter-version extensions can be used not only for missing elements, but also for missing datatypes, target resource differences, and cardinality changes, with additional expectations for Basic, version selection, vocabulary bindings, and denormalization.
initial_application: Commit 7e0b2667a232a9a92f16842ef6bfe306637fa432 applied the versions.html portions of the issue, adding guidance for target-resource handling, vocabulary-binding context, and simple-type mapping. Commit 0d7712ab28ac0b7410f8ae66c8358cbadba32eff added the requested Basic STU note the same day, though without the Jira key in the subject.
additional_context: Current source/versions.html was later refactored by f45505e5b3aa0d87effb991938750e627b782d2d to remove detailed cross-version examples and tables from core and point to individual cross-version definition packages. The active page still describes XVer extensions for elements that do not exist, datatypes that do not exist, and maximum-cardinality changes, and source/basic/basic-introduction.xml still carries the Basic note. Later related issues FHIR-44664 and FHIR-48379 added focused Basic canonical-resource and cardinality/FHIRPath guidance; FHIR-44616 remains only Resolved - change required and was used as context, not decided.
reconciliation: No source change was made. Re-adding the old detailed guidance to core would partially undo the later content move and duplicate guidance that now belongs with the XVer package/FAQ surface. Current FHIR-core source preserves the seed's essential implementer-facing scope and has no conflicting active build source requiring a FHIR-36702 fix.
